sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: New Yorkers are known to disagree about a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 纽约人出了名地对很多事情有分歧。

sentences.en: Who's got the best pizza?
sentences.zh: 谁家的披萨最好吃？

sentences.en: What's the fastest subway route?
sentences.zh: 哪条地铁路线最快？

sentences.en: Yankees or Mets?
sentences.zh: 洋基队还是大都会队？g

sentences.en: But I would bet that if you polled every New Yorker,
sentences.zh: 但我敢打赌，如果你民意调查每一个纽约人，

sentences.en: all 8,500,000 of them, they would agree on one thing.
sentences.zh: 所有八百五十万人，他们会在一件事上达成一致。

sentences.en: Penn Station sucks!
sentences.zh: 宾州车站糟透了！

sentences.en: That's Ann Hepperman, our friend and reporter in New York who also hates Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 那是安·海珀曼，我们驻纽约的朋友兼记者，她也讨厌宾州车站。

sentences.en: There is nothing joyful about Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 宾州车站里没有任何快乐可言。

sentences.en: It's windowless, airless, crowded.
sentences.zh: 这里没有窗户，没有空气，而且拥挤不堪。

sentences.en: 650,000 people have to suffer through it on their daily commute.
sentences.zh: 六十五万人在他们日常的通勤中不得不饱受其苦。

sentences.en: That's more traffic than the region's three airports combined.
sentences.zh: 这比该地区三个机场加起来的客流量还要多。

sentences.en: Luckily, though, I'm not one of them.
sentences.zh: 不过幸运的是，我不是其中之一。

sentences.en: We're in Penn Station now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在就在宾州车站。

sentences.en: We tagged along with our unlucky friend Jonathan Minjivar.
sentences.zh: 我们跟着我们倒霉的朋友乔纳森·明吉瓦尔一起去了。

sentences.en: He's a producer for This American Life and commutes from his home in Jersey to Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 他是《This American Life》的制作人，每天从他在泽西的家通勤到宾州车站。

sentences.en: His experience of Penn Station is like being at a Black Friday sale at Walmart.
sentences.zh: 他在宾州车站的体验就像是在沃尔玛赶黑色星期五大促销。

sentences.en: Every day.
sentences.zh: 每天如此。

sentences.en: Always.
sentences.zh: 总是这样。

sentences.en: And, like, the whole time people are pushing you.
sentences.zh: 而且，差不多全程都有人在推搡你。

sentences.en: Squeezing through a tiny stairway to get down to the tracks.
sentences.zh: 从一条极窄的楼梯挤下去才能到达站台。

sentences.en: It's the only place in which people are, like, actually touching your ass.
sentences.zh: 这是唯一一个人们会，怎么说呢，真的摸到你屁股的地方。

sentences.en: And you're not supposed to say anything about it.
sentences.zh: 而你还不能对此说什么。

sentences.en: The air is often hot and stuffy.
sentences.zh: 这里的空气通常又热又闷。

sentences.en: It feels like whatever Wizard of Oz is behind, like, that they are just watching in their little tower and watching, like, oh, look at them crush each other.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像不管是什么绿野仙踪在背后，比如说，他们只是在他们的小塔里看着，看着，哦，看他们互相挤压。

sentences.en: Look at them want to eat each other.
sentences.zh: 看他们恨不得把对方吃掉。

sentences.en: It's awful.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It's awful.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And it's my best way to get home every day.
sentences.zh: 而这是我每天回家最好的路线。

sentences.en: Poor guy.
sentences.zh: 可怜的家伙。

sentences.en: And you can also see some Penn Station hate in popular culture about New York.
sentences.zh: 你也可以在关于纽约的流行文化中看到一些对宾州车站的厌恶。

sentences.en: Like in this episode of Broad City, where one character, Abby, gets dumped because her boyfriend would rather end a relationship than take a train out of Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 就像在《大城小妞》这一集里，其中一个角色艾比被甩了，因为她的男友宁愿结束一段恋情，也不愿坐从宾州车站出发的火车。

sentences.en: Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 宾州车站。

sentences.en: I can't.
sentences.zh: 我受不了。

sentences.en: It's disgusting.
sentences.zh: 太令人作呕了。

sentences.en: It's kind of a deal breaker for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说这有点像是不可妥协的底线。

sentences.en: But here's the worst thing about Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 但关于宾州车站，最糟糕的是这个。

sentences.en: This drab, low-ceilinged, uninspiring, unexceptional building was once the opposite of all of those things.
sentences.zh: 这座单调、低矮、毫无灵感、平庸至极的建筑，曾经是所有这些的反面。

sentences.en: It was a vast space.
sentences.zh: 那是一个极其广阔的空间。

sentences.en: I mean, the building itself was the fourth largest building in the world when it was finished.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这座建筑本身在建成时是世界第四大建筑。

sentences.en: That's Jill Jones describing the original Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 这是吉尔·琼斯对最初的宾州车站的描述。

sentences.en: She wrote a great book about it called Conquering Gotham.
sentences.zh: 她写了一本关于它的优秀书籍，名为《征服哥谭》。

sentences.en: The original Penn Station in New York City opened in 1910.
sentences.zh: 纽约市最初的宾州车站于1910年开业。

sentences.en: It was majestic.
sentences.zh: 它雄伟壮丽。

sentences.en: Imagine the Parthenon, but for trains.
sentences.zh: 想象一下帕特农神庙，但它是为火车建造的。

sentences.en: The facade was a line of massive Doric columns.
sentences.zh: 其正面是一排巨大的多立克柱。

sentences.en: You'd walk through them, descend down a grand staircase, and into a waiting room designed to remind you of a Roman temple.
sentences.zh: 你穿过它们，沿着宏伟的楼梯走下去，进入一个旨在让你想起罗马神庙的候车室。

sentences.en: With these very high ceilings and very spectacular light coming through.
sentences.zh: 有着极高的天花板和透过它们照进来的极其壮观的光线。

sentences.en: And that ushered you into all of these staircases that took you down into the train tracks.
sentences.zh: 这把你引向所有那些带你通往火车站台的楼梯。

sentences.en: And the guy behind all of this was Alexander Cassatt, the head of Pennsylvania Railroad.
sentences.zh: 这一切背后的家伙是宾夕法尼亚铁路公司的负责人亚历山大·卡萨特。

sentences.en: With the original Penn Station, Cassatt was fixing a problem that had plagued New York for years.
sentences.zh: 通过最初的宾州车站，卡萨特解决了一个困扰纽约多年的问题。

sentences.en: Namely, it was a complete pain in the ass to get from New Jersey to Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，从新泽西到曼哈顿简直是个天大的麻烦。

sentences.en: People commuting from Jersey had to schlep across the Hudson River on a slow ferry.
sentences.zh: 从泽西通勤的人们必须坐着慢速渡轮费力地穿过哈德逊河。

sentences.en: So Cassatt built the first ever train tunnel to run under the Hudson River.
sentences.zh: 因此，卡萨特建造了有史以来第一条从哈德逊河下方穿过的铁路隧道。

sentences.en: It was considered one of the greatest engineering feats ever.
sentences.zh: 这被认为是历史上最伟大的工程壮举之一。

sentences.en: I know we say that all the time, but we really mean it this time.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们总是这么说，但这次我们是认真的。

sentences.en: And Cassatt built Penn Station Terminal to crown his monumental achievement.
sentences.zh: 卡萨特建造了宾州车站航站楼来为他这座不朽的成就加冕。

sentences.en: The architecture celebrated both the past and the future.
sentences.zh: 这种建筑风格既赞美了过去，也赞美了未来。

sentences.en: It was a combination of this very ancient grandeur and this extremely industrialized form of transportation.
sentences.zh: 它是这种极具古代宏伟气势与这种极其工业化运输形式的结合。

sentences.en: These really powerful trains.
sentences.zh: 这些威力强大的火车。

sentences.en: Newspapers called Penn Station the eighth wonder of the world.
sentences.zh: 报纸称宾州车站为世界第八大奇迹。

sentences.en: People call a lot of things the eighth wonder of the world, but we really mean it this time.
sentences.zh: 人们把很多东西都叫做世界第八大奇迹，但这次我们真的是认真的。

sentences.en: Everyone loved it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都喜欢它。

sentences.en: Everyone that is, except for one other railroad family that owned a little station right across town.
sentences.zh: 可以说是每个人，除了城另一头拥有一个小车站的另一个铁路家族。

sentences.en: This then made the existing Grand Central Station, which was owned by the Vanderbilt family, look really shabby.
sentences.zh: 这使得由范德比尔特家族拥有的现存中央车站显得非常破旧。

sentences.en: At the time when the original Penn Station was built, Grand Central Station was not anywhere near as grand as it is now.
sentences.zh: 在最初的宾州车站建造时，中央车站远没有现在这么宏伟。

sentences.en: But the Vanderbilts just couldn't be outdone by this other train station.
sentences.zh: 但范德比尔特家族就是不能被这个别的火车站比下去。

sentences.en: Clearly.
sentences.zh: 显然。

sentences.en: How embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 多尴尬啊。

sentences.en: So when Grand Central needed a little touch-up, the Vanderbilts decided to tear it down and build a newer, shinier, grander Grand Central Station.
sentences.zh: 所以当中央车站需要一点小修缮时，范德比尔特家族决定将其拆除，建造一个更新、更闪亮、更宏伟的中央车站。

sentences.en: The one we know today.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们今天所知道的那个。

sentences.en: So there was this very early connection between the two.
sentences.zh: 所以这两者之间很早就有了这种联系。

sentences.en: So Penn Station and Grand Central started out as enemies.
sentences.zh: 因此，宾州车站和中央车站一开始是死敌。

sentences.en: But as the years passed, they were like the last two drunks at the party trying to keep the night from coming to an end.
sentences.zh: 但随着岁月的流逝，它们就像派对上最后两个试图让黑夜不要结束的酒鬼。

sentences.en: The country was in a very different sort of mindset that new was good and flying was good and cars were good and trains were bad.
sentences.zh: 这个国家处于一种截然不同的心态中：新的就是好的，飞行是好的，汽车是好的，火车是坏的。

sentences.en: Penn Station was only 40 years old at this point, but already its days were numbered.
sentences.zh: 此时的宾州车站只有四十岁，但它的日子已经屈指可数了。

sentences.en: After World War II, passenger trains just weren't as popular anymore.
sentences.zh: 二战后，客运列车不再那么受欢迎了。

sentences.en: Pennsylvania Railroad was just bleeding money.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚铁路公司简直在流血亏损。

sentences.en: The company couldn't afford the upkeep of Penn Station's grandeur.
sentences.zh: 该公司无力承担维护宾州车站宏伟气势的费用。

sentences.en: Everything that had been glorious about it really got sort of covered with grime and it was dirty and they didn't fix the broken windows and there were all these pigeons flying around.
sentences.zh: 所有曾经辉煌的东西真的都蒙上了污垢，而且很脏，他们不修理破损的窗户，周围到处都是飞来飞去的鸽子。

sentences.en: It's really hard to wash pigeon poop off a four-story arch glass ceiling.
sentences.zh: 要把鸽子粪从四层楼高的拱形玻璃天花板上洗掉真的很难。

sentences.en: So people did not feel that this was this glorious place.
sentences.zh: 所以人们并不觉得这是一个辉煌的地方。

sentences.en: They felt it was really crummy.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得这里真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: For a lot of people, Penn Station had become a money-sucking albatross of a station.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，宾州车站已经变成了一个吞噬金钱、形同信天翁般的累赘车站。

sentences.en: That also sat on nine acres of precious midtown Manhattan real estate.
sentences.zh: 它还占据着曼哈顿中城九英亩宝贵的黄金地段。

sentences.en: Remember, this is New York City.
sentences.zh: 记住，这是纽约市。

sentences.en: Real estate in New York is in the airspace.
sentences.zh: 纽约的房地产在于其领空权。

sentences.en: Pennsylvania Railroad executives knew that they could make tons of money if they could rent out the space above the station to a big, tall building.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚铁路公司的高管们知道，如果他们能把车站上方的空间租给一座高大宏伟的建筑，他们就能赚大笔钱。

sentences.en: There were proposals to build a parking garage, amphitheaters, a 40-story office tower.
sentences.zh: 曾有提案建造停车场、露天剧场和四十层的办公大楼。

sentences.en: But the one that won out was the futuristic sports and entertainment palace known as Madison Square Garden.
sentences.zh: 但最终胜出的是被称为麦迪逊广场花园的未来主义体育和娱乐殿堂。

sentences.en: The deal that Pennsylvania Railroad cut with the developer, Irving Feltz, was to keep the tracks below Penn Station and sell the rights to the airspace on top.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚铁路公司与开发商欧文·费尔茨达成的交易是保留宾州车站下方的轨道，并出售上方领空的开发权。

sentences.en: And blow up Penn Station in the process.
sentences.zh: 并在这一过程中炸毁了宾州车站。

sentences.en: Here's where I wish we could say that the whole city banded together to save the station.
sentences.zh: 这就是我希望我们能说整个城市联合起来拯救车站的时候。

sentences.en: But actually, no one really cared.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，根本没人真正在乎。

sentences.en: Except for a small group of activist architects.
sentences.zh: 除了极少数激进派建筑师。

sentences.en: Agbeni.
sentences.zh: 阿格贝尼。

sentences.en: The Action Group for Better Architecture in New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约更好建筑行动小组。

sentences.en: So, Agbeni.
sentences.zh: 也就是 Agbeni。

sentences.en: It's a terrible acronym.
sentences.zh: 这是一个糟糕的缩写。

sentences.en: But definitely a cause I can support.
sentences.zh: 但绝对是一个我能支持的事业。

sentences.en: Peter Sampton was one of those architects.
sentences.zh: 彼得·萨姆普顿就是那些建筑师之一。

sentences.en: I went over to his house on the Upper West Side.
sentences.zh: 我去了他在上西区的家。

sentences.en: And we looked through old photographs from the only march to save Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 我们翻阅了唯一的拯救宾州车站游行活动的老照片。

sentences.en: Excuse me.
sentences.zh: 对不起。

sentences.en: I think this was my sign right here that said,
sentences.zh: 我想这就在这里，是我的牌子，上面写着，

sentences.en: Don't sell our city short.
sentences.zh: 不要低估我们的城市。

sentences.en: The date was August 2nd, 1962.
sentences.zh: 日期是1962年8月2日。

sentences.en: There were 200 rowdy architects.
sentences.zh: 有两百名喧闹的建筑师。

sentences.en: We would have to wear respectable clothing.
sentences.zh: 我们必须穿着得体的衣服。

sentences.en: Because otherwise they wouldn't take us seriously.
sentences.zh: 因为否则他们不会认真对待我们。

sentences.en: Just kidding about the rowdy part.
sentences.zh: 开玩笑的，关于喧闹的那部分。

sentences.en: These were architects.
sentences.zh: 这些都是建筑师。

sentences.en: The men wore suits.
sentences.zh: 男士们穿着西装。

sentences.en: The women wore white gloves and pearls.
sentences.zh: 女士们戴着白手套和珍珠项链。

sentences.en: We each sort of prided ourselves on doing better lettering than the next sign.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都以比隔壁标语写得更好而自豪。

sentences.en: They marched up and down 7th Avenue shouting,
sentences.zh: 他们沿着第七大道游行，大声喊着，

sentences.en: Polish, don't demolish, save our heritage.
sentences.zh: 擦亮，不要拆毁，拯救我们的遗产。

sentences.en: Things like that is what we would say.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的话就是我们会说的。

sentences.en: I mean, keep in mind, none of us were ever on a picket line before.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，记住，我们以前从来没有人参加过纠察线。

sentences.en: You don't say.
sentences.zh: 可不是吗。

sentences.en: Still, the protest made the front page of the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，这场抗议还是登上了《纽约时报》的头版。

sentences.en: Architects fight Penn Station plan.
sentences.zh: 建筑师反对宾州车站计划。

sentences.en: But it was too late.
sentences.zh: 但为时已晚。

sentences.en: On October 28th, 1963, at 9 a.m.,
jackhammers tore into Penn Station's granite slabs.
sentences.zh: 风镐凿入了宾州车站的花岗岩板。

sentences.en: The demolition took a long time.
sentences.zh: 拆除工作花了很长时间。

sentences.en: About three years.
sentences.zh: 大约三年。

sentences.en: You know, it was like a great animal because you saw the black of the outside
sentences.zh: 你知道，它就像一头巨大的动物，因为你看到了外面的黑色，

sentences.en: and then you saw the inside, which was all this beautiful pink.
sentences.zh: 然后你看到了里面，全都是这种美丽的粉红色。

sentences.en: So it was like the flesh was opened up with a knife.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉就像血肉被刀子剖开了一样。

sentences.en: And after three years, most of the original Penn Station's remains,
sentences.zh: 三年后，最初宾州车站的大部分遗迹，

sentences.en: the dork columns, the granite and travertine details,
sentences.zh: 多立克柱、花岗岩和石灰华细节，

sentences.en: all of that had been dumped into a New Jersey swamp.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都被倒进了一个新泽西的沼泽里。

sentences.en: And of course, they gave us a new Penn Station,
sentences.zh: 当然，他们给了我们一个新的宾州车站，

sentences.en: one that was summarily hated by everyone.
sentences.zh: 一个受到所有人一致唾弃的车站。

sentences.en: In 1968, architectural historian Vincent Scully famously remarked that,
sentences.zh: 1968年，建筑历史学家文森特·斯库利有一句名言：

sentences.en: whereas before one entered the city like a god,
sentences.zh: 过去人们如神明般进入这座城市，

sentences.en: one scuttles in now like a rat.
sentences.zh: 而现在人们如老鼠般仓皇钻入。

sentences.en: After the destruction of Penn Station,
sentences.zh: 在宾州车站被毁之后，

sentences.en: Mayor Robert Wagner created the first Landmarks Preservation Commission.
sentences.zh: 市长罗伯特·瓦格纳创建了第一个地标保护委员会。

sentences.en: And in 1965, the group helped pass the city's first ever Landmarks Law,
sentences.zh: 并在1965年，该组织帮助通过了该市有史以来的第一部地标法，

sentences.en: so that something as drastic as the destruction of Penn Station could never happen again.
sentences.zh: 这样像毁灭宾州车站那样激烈的事件就再也不会发生了。

sentences.en: But the Landmark Laws were flawed.
sentences.zh: 但《地标法》是有缺陷的。

sentences.en: It was a joke.
sentences.zh: 这简直是个笑话。

sentences.en: New Yorkers are so blunt.
sentences.zh: 纽约人就是这么直言不讳。

sentences.en: That's Roberta Gratz.
sentences.zh: 那是罗伯塔·格拉茨。

sentences.en: She wrote award-winning stories about the problems with the city's Landmark Laws
sentences.zh: 她写过关于该市地标法问题的获奖报道

sentences.en: The biggest one, though, was that the Landmarks Commission didn't meet all that much.
sentences.zh: 然而最大的问题是，地标委员会开会的频率并不高。

sentences.en: They met for six months, every three years.
sentences.zh: 他们每三年会面一次，持续六个月。

sentences.en: So if you missed your window to get your favorite New York City building landmarked,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你错过了为心仪的纽约市建筑争取地标保护的机会，

sentences.en: tough luck.
sentences.zh: 那就真倒霉了。

sentences.en: And in the meantime,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，

sentences.en: the bulldozer operated at will.
sentences.zh: 推土机随心所欲地运作着。

sentences.en: Gratz says a lot of buildings were lost even after the Landmark Laws were passed.
